title: Invaract Organizational Contract Policy
description: Structural shape of an organizational policy document Invaract's `contract` module (com.invaract.contract.OrgPolicyParser/OrgPolicyValidator) accepts - a platform-owned artifact, separate from any one contract, expressing rules that apply across every contract in an organization (see docs/CONTRACT_MODEL.md's "Organizational Policy" section). Attached to a Spark job via the `spark.invaract.orgPolicy` conf key (spark-adapter's ContractEnforcementRule), independent of any change to the job's own source. Deliberately permissive (`additionalProperties: true`) on policy-rule-specific properties, since each rule `type`'s own extra keys (e.g. `technology` for `require_catalog`, `name`/`fieldType` for `require_field`, `pattern` for `field_naming_convention`, `key`/`value` for `require_extension`, `formats` for `require_format`, `ifKey`/`ifValue`/`thenKey`/`thenValue` for `require_extension_if`; `require_dataset_description` takes none) are open-ended, decoded by OrgPolicyParser rather than fixed here - the same layering invaract-contract.schema.json uses for `rules`. `require_field`'s type pin is deliberately `fieldType`, not `type`: a policy rule's own kind is itself the `type` key at the same mapping level.

version.description: Free-form revision identifier for this policy document itself - not compared against ContractVersion semantics, just tracked like any other version-controlled config.

policies.description: The policy rules themselves. Eight types are interpreted today (com.invaract.contract.PolicyType/PolicyRule.interpret): 'require_catalog' (optional 'technology'), 'require_field' (required 'name', optional 'fieldType'), 'field_naming_convention' (required 'pattern', a regex every field name - recursing into nested struct fields - must fully match), 'require_extension' (required 'key', optional 'value' - checks the contract's own top-level 'extensions' map, e.g. requiring every contract to declare an 'owner'; unlike the dataset-level types, this checks the contract as a whole once, not once per dataset, so 'scope'/'when' have no effect on it - OrgPolicyValidator warns if they're set), 'require_format' (required 'formats' - a single format string or a list, e.g. 'delta' or ['delta', 'iceberg'] - matched case-insensitively against the dataset's own declared 'format'), 'require_dataset_description' (no properties - the dataset's own 'description' must simply be present and non-blank), 'require_dataset_type' (optional 'types' - a single DATA_ASSET/SOURCE/CONTROL value or a list; the dataset's own 'type' must be declared at all, and if 'types' is set, must be one of them - this is the mechanism that makes declaring a dataset's 'type' mandatory or optional per organization, since Dataset.datasetType itself always defaults to unset), and 'require_extension_if' (required 'ifKey'/'thenKey', optional 'ifValue'/'thenValue' - a conditional require_extension: only when the contract already satisfies 'ifKey'[='ifValue'] must it also satisfy 'thenKey'[='thenValue'], e.g. a contract with extensions.status=deprecated must also declare extensions.sunsetDate; a contract not satisfying the 'if' condition is unaffected, and like require_extension this is contract-wide, so 'scope'/'when' are inert on it too). A known type with malformed properties for its shape is an OrgPolicyValidator Error; a type outside this set is checked via 'customPolicyTypes' (below) if it names a CustomPolicyEvaluator for it, otherwise it's recorded but never checked (interpret returns None), the same permissive behavior ContractRule.interpret has for an unrecognized contract rule type.

inject.description: Rules/options this policy contributes to every contract it governs, merged in before verification runs - so an org-wide requirement (e.g. 'no unconditional DELETE anywhere') doesn't depend on every contract author remembering to declare it themselves.

exemptions.description: Platform-controlled exceptions - a contract's own author cannot exempt their own contract; only whoever owns this policy file can. Each exemption is scoped to specific policy ids and can carry an expiry ('reviewBy'); an exemption whose reviewBy has passed no longer applies (OrgPolicyValidator warns, it does not error).

customPolicyTypes.description: Maps a policy rule 'type' name this document uses to the fully-qualified class name of a com.invaract.contract.CustomPolicyEvaluator implementation that evaluates it - the reflective, no-source-change extension point for an organizational policy type outside the eight built-in ones described above, resolved by com.invaract.contract.CustomPolicyEvaluatorFactory the same way spark-adapter's NotificationSinkFactory already resolves a notification sink.class. A key here that collides with one of the eight built-in types is dead (the built-in interpretation always wins) and is flagged by OrgPolicyValidator as a Warning, not an Error; a policy rule whose 'type' matches neither a built-in type nor an entry here is also flagged (Warning) as a rule that will never be evaluated; a class name here that doesn't resolve (missing class, no public no-arg constructor, doesn't implement CustomPolicyEvaluator) is an Error.

typeGuarantees.description: Configures com.invaract.contract.TypeGuaranteeValidator's cross-contract 'stronger semantic and guarantee validation' checks (docs/CONTRACT_MODEL.md's "Type guarantee checks" section) - the DATA_ASSET/SOURCE/CONTROL type system's Phase 6. Unlike every other key in this document, this is not consumed by OrgPolicyEvaluator/ContractEnforcementRule against one contract at a time: com.invaract.contract.cli.CrossContractLintCli's own '--org-policy' flag reads only this block from the named document and runs it across every contract the lint run discovers together. Omitted entirely, no type guarantee check runs at all - the same 'absent means off' default every other opt-in capability in this schema follows.

id.description: Stable identifier for this policy rule, referenced by exemptions and shown in violation messages. Must be unique among this document's policies (OrgPolicyValidator errors on a duplicate).

type.description: Policy kind - see the top-level 'policies' description for the eight types Invaract currently interprets.

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation, surfaced in violation messages for self-service remediation.

scope.description: Which of a contract's datasets this policy applies to.

when.description: Optionally narrows which datasets this policy applies to, beyond 'scope' alone.

mode.description: 'enforce' blocks - ContractEnforcementRule throws before any Spark plan is analyzed. 'warn' only publishes a notification event, letting a new policy be rolled out safely (watched, then flipped to 'enforce') before it starts blocking jobs.

sensitivityTag.description: Only datasets with at least one field (recursively, through nested struct properties) carrying this sensitivity tag are in scope for this policy - see Field.sensitivityTags.

rules.description: ContractRule-shaped entries (the same 'type' + properties shape a contract's own 'rules' key uses) merged into every governed contract's rules before RuleVerifier runs.

minVerificationOptions.description: Floors ORed onto VerificationOptions (e.g. rejectUndeclaredFields, rejectUndeclaredInputs, computeFingerprint) - a flag a job's own code left false can still be forced true by policy; the reverse never happens.

enabled.description: Which type guarantee checks to run, by com.invaract.contract.TypeGuaranteeType name. Two are built in: 'data_asset_schema_consistency' (every DATA_ASSET declared at the same physical location, across every contract discovered together, must agree on schema - a mismatch is Contradicts) and 'data_asset_downstream_consumption' (a DATA_ASSET output not declared as an input anywhere else is CannotDetermine, never Contradicts - Invaract cannot prove a contract nobody has written yet will never consume it). A name that is neither built in nor a 'customTypeGuaranteeTypes' key is recorded but never evaluated (OrgPolicyValidator warns, it does not error) - the same forward-compatible, typo-tolerant behavior 'customPolicyTypes' already has for an unrecognized policy rule 'type'. Empty or omitted means no type guarantee check runs at all.

mode.description: 'enforce': a Contradicts result from any enabled check blocks the CrossContractLintCli run (non-zero exit). 'warn': every enabled check still runs and is reported, but a Contradicts result never blocks - the same enforce/warn distinction 'policyRule.mode' already draws, applied here to the whole typeGuarantees block rather than per-check, since these checks are inherently cross-contract, not scoped to one contract's own policyRule.

customTypeGuaranteeTypes.description: Maps a check name used in 'enabled' to the fully-qualified class name of a com.invaract.contract.TypeGuaranteeCheck implementation that runs it - the reflective, no-source-change extension point for a type guarantee check beyond the two built in, resolved by com.invaract.contract.TypeGuaranteeCheckFactory the same way 'customPolicyTypes' is resolved by CustomPolicyEvaluatorFactory. A key here that collides with a built-in TypeGuaranteeType is dead (the built-in check always wins) and is flagged by OrgPolicyValidator as a Warning, not an Error; a class name here that doesn't resolve (missing class, no public no-arg constructor, doesn't implement TypeGuaranteeCheck) is an Error.

contractId.description: The Contract.id this exemption applies to.

policyIds.description: Which policy rule ids (see policyRule.id, above) this exemption covers.

reason.description: Why this exemption exists - required, for auditability.

reviewBy.description: Optional ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which this exemption stops applying. Omitted means the exemption never expires.
